source.title: Co-teaching: Robust training of deep neural networks with extremely noisy labels
source.authors: Bo Han; Quanming Yao; Xingrui Yu; Gang Niu; Miao Xu; Weihua Hu; I. Tsang; Masashi Sugiyama

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates test accuracy under simulated label corruption, a related measure of the noisy-label behavior in V4. It does not measure training error on random labels.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior memorization findings, but those citations are not its own results. Its Standard baseline reports test accuracy for three datasets and three structured noise settings; it does not report training error for Standard. The Co-teaching results are a new method and are not cataloged as results of the claim's object.
record.test_reason: Standard-network results bear on V4's test-performance component: increasing symmetric corruption from 20% to 50% lowers test accuracy on all three datasets. The paper also reports its own temporal evidence relevant to V6: Standard's MNIST test accuracy initially rises and subsequently declines, explicitly interpreted as memorization. Neither result establishes perfect training-set fitting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the main conclusion: Co-teaching improves robustness under the tested simulated noisy-label conditions, with theoretical guarantees and generalization analysis left for future work. However, the record's separate assertion that V6 appears only through citations is incorrect: the authors explicitly interpret their own Standard test-accuracy trajectories as evidence of memorization.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains with structured simulated label corruption and evaluates test accuracy; it does not reproduce the original random-label fitting experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and corruption type/rate vary across the reported Standard test-accuracy results.
record.peer_reviewed: 32nd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2018), Montréal, Canada
record.problems: For the Standard baseline, the paper reports test accuracy but not training error. The tested corruptions are structured pair or symmetric flips rather than a fully random labeling, and the cited memorization findings are prior work.
record.rows_left_out: Co-teaching and other method rows in Tables 4–6 are results of the paper's proposed method or comparators, not results for the claim's standard-network object. Epoch-wise Standard test-accuracy curves in Figures 3, 5, and 6 are figure-only and are not separately extracted because the tables report the Standard endpoint test accuracy for each condition.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training error on completely random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters relative to true-label training.
Relative training time and convergence speed as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training-set fitting, steady degradation over the full none-to-all corruption range, and arrival at chance performance. Pair flipping is tested at only one rate.
Regularization ablations establishing whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevents random-label fitting or is necessary for true-label generalization.
Direct measurements of clean-label versus corrupted-label training accuracy or loss over time, and a separate fully random-label learning trajectory.

missing.what: Represent Standard's initially high and subsequently declining MNIST test accuracy as temporal evidence for V6. The record declares epoch curves omitted, but incorrectly treats their V6 relevance as only a citation to prior work; endpoint rows cannot capture this result.
missing.locator: Section 4.1, Results on MNIST, paragraph discussing Figure 3; Figure 3(a–c).

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. All nine endpoint values and uncertainties match the supplied tables. Two symmetric noise rates support only a test-degradation component; missing training-error measurements are untested portions, not evidence against the claim. The V6 evidence is indirect and does not independently establish which individual labels were fitted first.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks reach zero or near-zero training error on completely random labels, and whether their test error is at chance.
Training time relative to true labels and convergence speed as corruption rises.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

The paper tests structured pair and symmetric label flips at 20%, 45%, and 50%, but does not report Standard training error, test error across the full none-to-all range, or a trend over that full range.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation affect fitting random labels or generalization on true labels.
Whether the paper's own networks learn shared real-label patterns before memorizing noise; the paper cites prior work on this behavior.

relationships.condition: Standard CNNs on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100; symmetric corruption increased from 20% to 50%; test-performance component only.
relationships.reason: R3→R2, R6→R5, and R9→R8 show test accuracy falling from 94.05% to 66.05%, 76.25% to 48.87%, and 47.55% to 25.21%, respectively; perfect fitting and a continuous trend remain undetermined.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy fell from 94.05% to 66.05% on MNIST, 76.25% to 48.87% on CIFAR-10, and 47.55% to 25.21% on CIFAR-100.

relationships.condition: Standard CNN on MNIST under Pair-45%, Symmetry-50%, and Symmetry-20%; indirect temporal evidence.
relationships.reason: Based on Section 4.1 and Figure 3, rather than endpoint rows: the authors explicitly report an initial high test accuracy followed by decline in all three conditions, interpreting this as memorization; clean/noisy training-fit trajectories are not measured.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy was initially high and then declined in all three noise settings, which the authors interpreted as noisy-label memorization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
